subclaim: S2/S3 (weighted ratio estimator; Hajek reweighting) — sentence of §6.5 'inverse-frequency weighting does not reduce the RMSE in any of the four cells'
origem: requested in the internal review of the manuscript (the Hajek weighting used Monte Carlo frequencies, not the closed-form p_i); adopted on 03/10/2026
pergunta: Does Hajek reweighting with the CLOSED-FORM inclusion probability of each node (class m(i): closed form for m = 0, 1, 3; for m = 2 there are only bounds — use the empirical frequency of the class over 200 split draws, declared) reduce the RMSE of the reported error relative to the domain mean, against the unweighted estimator H, in the 4 Q1 cells, for the constant predictor and the calibrated FSPL (b), on the valid nodes and on all nodes?
desenho: same 200 split draws (split_seed) and same 92/20/20 partition (g = 10, b = 2) as fase4/R2 (scripts/v3_12_R2_referencia_desenho.py, reused by import without editing; sha checked); p_i = (k_te/N) * c(m_i), with c(0) = 1, c(1) = (k_te-1)/(N-1), c(3) = closed form from fase4/R4_p_por_classe.json (classes_nodais, valor_fechado), and c(2) = empirical frequency of the class over 200 split draws (R4), per cell; m_i = number of neighbouring blocks within b of the node (nodal class of R4, recomputed by the same function); J_fechado = sum(e_i/p_i)/sum(1/p_i) over the scored nodes of the split draw (no p_i = 0 by construction); reference mu_U = domain mean (R2); RMSE over the split draws with a valid node.
metricas: per cell, predictor, population: RMSE(J_fechado), RMSE(H), ratio RMSE(J_fechado)/RMSE(H); bias and Monte Carlo SE of J_fechado; validation: H recomputed equal to that of R2_resumo (==) and J with p = frequency over 200 (J_p200) equal to that of R2 (==); count of the cells with ratio < 1 and < 0.9.
leitura: constant/valid: ratio < 0.9 in >= 3 of the 4 cells -> DELIMITS the current sentence: 'reweighting with the truncated frequency does not reduce; with the closed-form probability it reduces the RMSE by X %' (citable number). ratio in [0.9; 1.1] in the 4 cells -> REINFORCES the current sentence, now with the closed-form p_i and with the value (citable): 'does not reduce (ratio 0.9-1.1)'. ratio > 1.1 in >= 3 -> likewise reinforces, with 'increases'. FSPL and all nodes: reported alongside.
se_inverter: no outcome inverts S2/S3 (the bias of the ratio estimator is an identity); only the sentence on reweighting changes.
orcamento: CPU; 4 cells x 200 split draws; ~15 min in the s33 venv (do the R2 partial results already carry per-draw indices? if not, recompute the partition: ~1 h).
